newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds eyes share repurchase from spinoff.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds eyes share repurchase from spinoff.

text.p: Reynolds Metals Co will probably use the money raised from spinning off its lucrative canmaking and packaging businesses to repurchase shares, Reynolds chairman and CEO Jeremiah Sheehan said.
Reynolds reiterated Wednesday it was looking to spin off cans and packaging together, sell one business or the other, or sell a portion of these two businesses.
What to do with packaging and cans will be decided before year-end, Sheehan told reporters following an company briefing with analysts.
Keeping the two divisions as they are was not an option.
"If we did such a sale, we probably would go to our board and ask for approval to make a share repurchase," Sheehan said.
He declined to say how much either of the two businesses would be worth if they went partly or all on the block.
Last year packaging and consumer products sales totaled $1.4 billion, with can sales a further $1.2 billion out of total company sales of $5.1 billion.

Reynolds intends to report results for all its six newly created business units in future. They are bauxite and alumina, metals and carbon products, transportation, construction and distribution, packaging and consumer, and cans.
Wall Street analysts have been pushing Reynolds for some time to spin off the packaging and can divisions, but Sheehan denied he was being forced to carry out their wishes.
"We are doing it to improve shareholder value," he said.
Reynolds' can sales rose just under four percent in the first half of the year with market share increasing.
The improvement in can sales to the soft drinks sector compensated for the erosion, now halted, of sales to beer companies, Sheehan said.
The aluminum beverage can has faced stiffer competition from glass in the beer sector and plastic bottles in soft drinks, analysts have said.
"The demise of the aluminum beverage can has been greatly exaggerated," Sheehan countered.
